headline: South Korea's financial regulator has circulated 28 internet addresses tied to hacking attempts presumed to involve AI agents and told financial firms to finish security self-checks by 8 Oct.
score_reason: Pool score kept: an official regulator notice with concrete numbers and a deadline; the AI-agent link is only presumed.
importance_line: Customers of South Korean banks and other financial firms, and the institutions that must now inspect their systems and block the flagged addresses, are affected, but the use of AI agents is only presumed, the addresses may not show where the attackers are because they were routed through many countries, and the regulator itself warns against over-reading the country data.
summary: Chosunbiz reports that on 6 Oct 2026 South Korea's Financial Supervisory Service, the financial regulator, circulated 33 internet addresses (28 after removing duplicates) tied to hacking attempts on the financial sector that are presumed to have used AI agents, and asked institutions to finish self-inspections and fixes by 8 Oct. This continues the story we carried on 5 Oct 2026 about seven financial companies hit by simultaneous attacks; new today are the address list, a 12-item checklist for firms and Toss Bank's finding of abnormal access from flagged addresses as early as January, while some in the cybersecurity industry suspect a China-origin attack and authorities have named no country.
notes: Read in full. Follow-up of the 5 Oct 2026 item on seven financial companies hit (pool 1005:C12-02). Same story line as C12-01 and C12-14.
